title: Stock Detail page: move the Insider Transactions block to the bottom of the page
description:
User-requested layout change, confirmed via reading the current code before writing this task: `StockDetailPage.tsx` renders `FundamentalDataPanel` (earnings/dividend dates, short interest, and -- as its own last `Card`, FundamentalDataPanel.tsx lines ~385-433 -- Insider Transactions + detected clusters) directly below `SignalSummary`, near the top of the page, ahead of `ScreensPanel`/`IndicatorsPanel`/`StockCharts`. `FundamentalDataPanel.tsx`'s own doc comment (lines ~200-209) explains this placement is deliberate specifically because of the earnings-date warning banner rendered inside the SAME panel -- 'the highest-value piece per this task's own description ... immediately visible near the top of the page rather than buried below several other panels and the price chart.' That rationale is about the earnings banner, NOT about the Insider Transactions card, which is simply the last thing rendered inside that panel today as an implementation detail of how the panel happens to be composed -- nothing in the doc comment or the task history says Insider Transactions itself needs to be near the top.

The user wants the Insider Transactions block specifically moved to the LAST block on the page (i.e. after `StockCharts`), while the earnings-warning-banner rationale for the REST of `FundamentalDataPanel` (the banner itself, Earnings Date / Ex-Dividend Date / Short Interest) must NOT be disturbed -- it stays near the top for the reason already documented.

This requires extracting the Insider Transactions card (the `InsiderClusterCallouts` component, the `insiderColumns`/`InsiderRow` table, and the surrounding `Card`/`CardContent` markup at the end of `FundamentalDataPanel.tsx`) into its own component -- e.g. a new `InsiderTransactionsPanel.tsx` alongside `FundamentalDataPanel.tsx` in `features/stocks/components/` -- rendered by `StockDetailPage.tsx` as the LAST element in its `Stack`, after `StockCharts`. `FundamentalDataPanel` keeps the warning banner plus the Earnings Date/Ex-Dividend Date/Short Interest stat cards, and drops its `insiderClusters` prop and the Insider Transactions `Card` entirely.

One edge case to handle deliberately, not silently: `FundamentalDataPanel`'s `unavailable_reason === 'fallback_provider_active'` early-return branch (lines ~232-263) currently covers insider-transactions unavailability too -- its message literally says '...and insider transactions aren't available...'. Once Insider Transactions becomes its own component, decide and record whether the new component needs its own equivalent 'fallback provider active, no insider data' empty state (consulting the same `extendedData.unavailable_reason` it's already passed), or some other treatment -- don't let that messaging silently disappear.

checklist.step: Re-read `FundamentalDataPanel.tsx` and `StockDetailPage.tsx` in full to confirm the current structure matches this task's description (source may have moved since this task was written).

Extract the Insider Transactions card (`InsiderClusterCallouts`, `insiderColumns`/`InsiderRow`, the trailing `Card`/`CardContent` block) into a new sibling component, preserving its existing `MetricHelp` content (`insiderClustersHelp`/`insiderTransactionsHelp`) and behavior exactly.

Decide and record how the new component handles `extendedData.unavailable_reason === 'fallback_provider_active'` (its own empty/unavailable state vs. some other treatment) so that messaging isn't silently dropped.

Wire the new component into `StockDetailPage.tsx` as the last block on the page (after `StockCharts`), passing `extendedData`/`insiderClusters` the same way `FundamentalDataPanel` currently receives them.

Update `FundamentalDataPanel.tsx`'s own prop types and doc comment (drop the `insiderClusters` prop and the now-inaccurate 'same card, stay visually grouped' rationale) and its unavailable-provider branch's copy (no longer needs to mention insider transactions in the same sentence).

Move/update existing tests: `FundamentalDataPanel.test.tsx`'s insider-related cases move to the new component's own test file; `StockDetailPage.test.tsx`'s assertions about block order are updated to match the new bottom placement.
Real-browser check confirming the Insider Transactions block visually renders last on the page, below the chart panes, with no change to the earnings-warning banner's own top-of-page prominence.

decisions.decision: Extracted the Insider Transactions card into a new `InsiderTransactionsPanel.tsx` component (features/stocks/components/) rendered by `StockDetailPage.tsx` as the last element in its `Stack`, after `StockCharts`. Gave it its own 'fallback provider active' unavailable empty state (a dashed-border Card naming the cause, mirroring `FundamentalDataPanel`'s own equivalent branch) rather than letting that messaging silently disappear or folding it back into `FundamentalDataPanel`'s branch. This required a new `insiderTransactionsUnavailableHelp` MetricHelp content entry (metricHelpContent.ts), separate from `fundamentalDataUnavailableHelp`, whose own copy was narrowed to drop its insider-transactions mention now that `FundamentalDataPanel` only renders earnings/dividend dates and short interest. Rejected alternatives: (a) silently dropping the insider-unavailable messaging entirely -- explicitly ruled out by the task description; (b) having `InsiderTransactionsPanel` render nothing in that state and relying on `FundamentalDataPanel`'s banner alone to convey it -- rejected because the two components are no longer adjacent on the page (one is now at the very bottom), so a user scrolling straight to the bottom block would see a misleading blank/empty-looking table state with no explanation; (c) reusing `fundamentalDataUnavailableHelp` as-is for the new component -- rejected because its copy explicitly named earnings/dividend/short-interest fields that `InsiderTransactionsPanel` doesn't render, which would be confusing copy for a reader of just that card.
decisions.rationale: Keeps the 'unsupported by the currently active provider, distinct from checked-and-found-nothing' distinction (the whole point of this branch, per `fundamentalDataUnavailableHelp`'s/`insiderTransactionsUnavailableHelp`'s own `elderContext`) visible at both the top-of-page fundamentals card and the bottom-of-page insider-transactions card independently, since after this move they're no longer visually or spatially linked the way they were when both lived inside one `FundamentalDataPanel` early-return.

comments.summary: Behavior-preserving extraction verified line-by-line: FundamentalDataPanel.tsx's earnings-warning banner and Earnings Date/Ex-Dividend Date/Short Interest cards are byte-for-byte untouched except for dropping the trailing Insider Transactions Card and the insiderClusters prop; its own 'fallback provider active' branch copy was correctly narrowed (no longer mentions insider transactions). No stale references to the old insiderClusters prop or the old in-panel InsiderClusterCallouts location remain anywhere (grepped frontend/src).

InsiderTransactionsPanel's own new 'fallback provider active' unavailable state is well-justified and non-duplicative: it's scoped to insider-transactions-only copy via a new insiderTransactionsUnavailableHelp MetricHelp entry, while fundamentalDataUnavailableHelp's copy was correctly narrowed to drop the insider-transactions mention it used to carry. Read both unavailable_reason branches directly -- no contradiction or duplication between the two cards' messaging.

Independent live-browser check (Playwright script driven against the actual running dev server, not just trusting the task's screenshot claim) confirms the Insider Transactions card (heading, cluster callouts, and table) renders as the genuine last block on the page, directly after StockCharts' final chart panes ('Short Interest' heading at ~605px, 'Insider Transactions' heading at ~3580px, nothing below the insider table), with the earnings-warning-banner/Earnings Date/Ex-Dividend Date/Short Interest cards unchanged near the top. No console errors, no failed/4xx+ network requests observed.

Non-blocking (code-review, filed as a follow-up task): the checklist item 'StockDetailPage.test.tsx's assertions about block order are updated to match the new bottom placement' is marked done, but the diff shows zero changes to that file, and it never had any DOM-order assertions to begin with -- so nothing actually locks the new bottom placement into the automated regression suite. The behavior itself is correct (confirmed above), but an accidental future revert of the render order would pass the full test suite silently. See frontend-stock-detail-insider-transactions-last-followups.

pr_decision.notes: Independently re-ran both suites: backend pytest+coverage 1618 passed/99.94% line coverage, frontend vitest 1042/1042 passed with 99.77%/99.05%/99.84%/99.81% stmts/branches/fns/lines -- both match pr-reviewer's reported numbers exactly. Skimmed the full diff myself: FundamentalDataPanel.tsx's remaining content (banner, Earnings Date/Ex-Dividend Date/Short Interest cards) is untouched beyond dropping the insider Card/prop and narrowing the fallback-provider copy; InsiderTransactionsPanel.tsx's extracted cluster-callout/table logic is byte-identical to what was removed, plus a reasonable new unavailable state. Ran my own independent Playwright check against a fresh dev server (backend :8000, frontend :5174): 'Insider Transactions' heading rendered last (~3712px) with its Card's bottom edge (~10719px) landing within 24px of the page's actual scrollHeight (~10743px) -- genuinely the last block, no console errors or failed requests. Confirmed StockDetailPage.test.tsx has zero diff and no order-assertion mechanism (compareDocumentPosition, etc.) existed before or after -- the filed non-blocking follow-up (frontend-stock-detail-insider-transactions-last-followups) is accurate, and I agree it's non-blocking: the behavior itself is independently verified twice now (pr-reviewer's browser check and mine), so the gap is a regression-prevention debt item, not a correctness or placement doubt.
